Class ScreenMatcher

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.ScreenMatcher
public final class ScreenMatcher extends Object
Which screens a registered-slot presence (or any screen-complete feature) applies to — the consumer-facing expression of inventory-screen parity's default-on, opt-out-per-screen rule.

The default (all()) is the full inventory-bearing screen family: every AbstractContainerScreen. Under parity that is the right default — a consumer registers intent once and it manifests everywhere it could. Naming specific screens is therefore an explicit narrowing, the inverse of the old footgun where .on(InventoryScreen) silently missed creative (siblings, not parent/child):

  • all() — every container screen (the default).
  • allExcept(Class...) — every container screen but the named ones (a deliberate exclusion, e.g. "not in creative").
  • only(Class...) — only the named screens (full narrowing).

Matching is by class ancestry — the same isAssignableFrom test ScreenPanelAdapter.matches(Class) uses — so naming a base class matches its subclasses. This is the one matching primitive parity reuses; it is not a second screen-matcher.

Immutable value type. Reuse one instance across presences freely.

    • allExcept

      public static ScreenMatcher allExcept(Class<?>... screens)
      Every inventory-bearing screen except the named ones (and their subclasses). The clean way to opt a slot out of a specific screen, e.g. allExcept(CreativeModeInventoryScreen.class).

    • only

      public static ScreenMatcher only(Class<?>... screens)
      Only the named screens (and their subclasses). Full narrowing — use when a slot genuinely belongs on a closed set of screens rather than everywhere.

    • matches

      public boolean matches(Class<?> screenClass)
      Whether this matcher applies to the given opened screen's class. The mixins already gate on AbstractContainerScreen, so ScreenMatcher.Mode.ALL is an unconditional yes.
